inputs.text: Any political transition in Cuba must be judged by whether ordinary people gain real power—not by how quickly wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors can acquire land and businesses. When people already facing poverty and limited property have little say, privatization risks turning their labor and home into assets for those with the deepest pockets. Residents’ rights to own, work, and shape their future must come first; otherwise, political change could simply replace one unequal arrangement with another.
